q: 1. An undesirable element to be avoided while fixing the alignment of the highway is .............
options: right angled crossing for bridges, culverts and level crossing
proximity to a place of worship
explain: Alignment should avoid places of worship, graveyards, or historical monuments to prevent social, religious, and legal complications during land acquisition.

q: 2. Minimum gradient to be adopted for a black top road is .............
explain: A minimum longitudinal gradient (usually 1 in 200 to 1 in 500) is required even in flat terrain to ensure efficient side-drainage.

q: 3. Super elevation + lateral friction should not be greater than .............
explain: The equilibrium formula for super-elevation is e + f = V² / 127R, where V is in kmph and R is in meters.

q: 4. Minimum super elevation provided is .............
options: not less than the grade of the road
not less than camber at the section
explain: If the calculated super-elevation is less than the camber of the road, the camber value itself is provided for drainage purposes.

q: 5. The normal elevation of driver's eye is .............
explain: For sight distance design, the height of the driver's eye is standardized at 1.2 meters (120 cm) above the pavement.
Weaving is a traffic maneuver where vehicles merging from one side must cross paths with vehicles diverging to the other side within a limited distance.

q: 7. An advantage of manual counting of traffic is .............
options: Permits traffic classification by the type of vehicle
it can be carried out for any length of time
explain: Human observers can easily differentiate between motorcycles, cars, trucks, and buses, which basic mechanical counters often cannot do.

q: 8. A disadvantage of mechanical counting of traffic is .............
options: it is unpopular in inclement weather
explain: Standard automatic counters (like pneumatic tubes) count axles but struggle to accurately classify the specific type of vehicle.

q: 9. Grade separation had the advantage of .............
options: number of points of conflicts is nil
explain: Grade separation (flyovers/underpasses) physically separates crossing traffic, thereby reducing the number of intersection conflict points to zero.

q: 10. A disadvantage of 'Diamond junction' is .............
options: no provision for easy right turn
explain: In a standard diamond interchange, right-turning vehicles must still cross oncoming traffic at the terminal intersections on the minor road.

q: 11. The full width of land acquired before finalizing a highway, alignment is known .............
explain: The Right of Way (ROW) is the total width of land acquired for the road, including the pavement, shoulders, and future expansion areas.

q: 12. The convexity provided to the carriageway between the crown and edge of the pavement, is known as .............
explain: Camber (or cross-slope) is the transverse convexity provided to ensure water drains off the road surface.

q: 13. On a pavement with parabolic camber, the angle of inclination of the vehicles will be .............
options: same at the edges as well as at the crown
explain: In a parabolic shape, the slope increases as you move from the center (crown) toward the edges, meaning vehicles at the edge are tilted more.

q: 14. The ability of a driver to stop the vehicle moving with the designed speed, depends upon
explain: Stopping ability is a function of the PIEV theory (Perception, Intellection, Emotion, Volition) and the mechanical condition of the vehicle's braking system.

q: 15. The distance travelled by a moving vehicle during perception and brake reaction times, is known as
explain: Lag distance is the distance covered during the total reaction time (t), calculated as v * t.

q: 16. Minimum stopping distance for moving vehicles on road with a design speed of 80 km/hour, is
explain: Using the SSD formula $v t + v^2 / (2gf)$, for a speed of 80 km/h and standard friction, the value approximates to 120 meters.

q: 17. If V is the velocity in km ph, t the brake reaction time in seconds and η the efficiency of the brakes, the stopping distance S of the vehicle, is
explain: This is a derivation of the SSD formula where 0.28V represents the conversion of km/h to m/s for the lag distance, and the second term accounts for braking distance adjusted for efficiency.

q: 18. Design of horizontal curves on highways, is based on
options: permissible friction on the road surface
explain: The design must balance centrifugal force against available friction and super-elevation based on the design speed.

q: 19. The type of curves generally provided on highways, is
explain: Highway alignment consists of horizontal curves (often with transition curves) and vertical curves (summit and valley).

q: 20. The radius of curvature provided along a transition curve, is
options: equal to the radius of circular curve
varying from infinity to the radius of circular curve
explain: A transition curve begins with a radius of infinity (straight line) and gradually decreases to the radius of the circular curve it meets.

q: 21. If a Lemniscate curve having an angle of deflection Δ, is transitional throughout, the maximum polar angle is
explain: As per the geometry of the Lemniscate used as a transition, the max polar angle is one-sixth of the deflection angle.

q: 22. In a right angle bend of a road provided with a transition throughout, the maximum polar angle will be
explain: For a $90^\circ$ bend, $\Delta = 90^\circ$. Max polar angle = $\Delta / 6 = 90 / 6 = 15^\circ$.

q: 23. Alignment of highways in hilly regions, is decided on
options: long stretch of very hard cutting
explain: Hill alignment is a balance of avoiding expensive cutting, bridge costs, and geological hazards.

q: 24. The usual width of parapet walls along Highways in hilly region, is
explain: 60 cm is the standard width for safety parapets along hill road edges.

q: 25. The minimum value of camber provided for thin bituminous surface hill road, is
explain: For thin bituminous surfaces, the IRC recommended camber is $2.5\%$.

q: 26. If N is the algebraic difference of grades, S is the minimum sight distance in metres, the length (L) of a summit curve is
explain: When L > S, the length of a summit curve for stopping sight distance is calculated as L = NS²/4.4 (often simplified to NS²/4 in older textbooks).

q: 27. Retaining walls are generally constructed with dry rubble stones with 60 cm top width and
explain: A front batter of 1:4 (1 horizontal to 4 vertical) is common for dry rubble masonry retaining walls to ensure stability.

q: 28. Parapet walls along hill roads, are provided
options: to prevent the hill from sliding
to prevent the wheels of the vehicle from coming on the retaining wall
explain: Parapet walls serve as a safety barrier to keep vehicles from running off the edge of the road or onto the top of the retaining wall.

q: 29. For clear distinct vision, images of obstructions should fall on the retina with a cone of
explain: Acute vision is limited to a small central field of view, generally cited as a 3-degree cone in traffic psychology.

q: 30. Design of horizontal and vertical alignments, super-elevation, sight distance and grades, is worst affected by
explain: Speed is the most dominant variable in geometric design; it dictates the required radius of curves, the rate of super-elevation, and the necessary stopping distance.

q: 31. Road makers along roads from the edge of a kerb should not be less than
explain: A minimum lateral clearance of 60 cm is maintained from the kerb to any vertical signpost or marker to avoid being struck by vehicle mirrors.

q: 32. From the point of tangency before an intersection, the route markers are fixed at a distance of
explain: Advanced route markers are placed well ahead of the intersection (100–150m) to give drivers time to change lanes safely.

q: 33. The top height of a route marker above crown level is
explain: A standard height of 1.75 meters ensures the sign is within the driver's line of sight without being obscured by low-hanging foliage.

q: 34. The minimum ratio of the radii of two circular curves of a compound curve, is kept ............
explain: To ensure a smooth transition in a compound curve, the ratio of the larger radius to the smaller radius should ideally not exceed 1.5.

q: 35. The slope of the line joining the crown and edge of the road surface is known as ............
explain: Cross-fall, cross-slope, and camber are all terms used to describe the transverse slope provided for drainage.

q: 36. In scanty rainfall areas, the camber provided will be ............
explain: Since there is less water to drain, a flatter (gentler) camber can be used, which is more comfortable for high-speed travel.

q: 37. The camber of road should be approximately equal to ............ the longitudinal gradient.
explain: As a general rule of thumb for drainage, the cross slope (camber) is often half the value of the ruling longitudinal gradient.

q: 38. The stopping sight distance depends upon the ............
explain: SSD is influenced by the total reaction time of the driver, the speed of the vehicle, and the efficiency of the brakes (braking distance).

q: 39. The reason for providing curves on a highway is ............
options: to provide access to a particular locality
restriction imposed by some unavoidable reasons of land
explain: Curves are used to navigate around obstacles, stay within property boundaries, or reach specific destinations while maintaining a continuous alignment.

q: 40. The factor which influences the design of curves, is ............
explain: Design speed determines the radius, while superelevation and the centrifugal ratio (P/W) ensure stability and comfort during the turn.

q: 41. A transition curve cannot be a ............
explain: Spirals and parabolas can function as transition curves because their radii change; a compound curve consists of two or more circular arcs with constant radii, so it is not a transition curve itself.

q: 42. The shape of a vertical curve is ............
explain: Parabolic curves are preferred for vertical alignments because they provide a constant rate of change of grade, which is ideal for comfort and sight distance.

q: 43. A wall constructed to retain the earth from slippage on the hill side of the roadway is called ............
explain: A breast wall is built on the uphill side to prevent the natural slope from sliding onto the road.

q: 44. The parapet walls are usually required on the valley side of the roadway, in order to ............
options: properly guide the vehicles to the roadway
explain: Parapet walls act as a safety barrier and visual guide for drivers to prevent vehicles from going off the edge on the valley side.

q: 45. The endoscope is used to determine ............
explain: An Enoscope (L-shaped mirror box) is a simple tool used by traffic engineers to measure spot speeds by timing vehicles over a short base distance.

q: 46. A complete signal-time cycle constitutes ............
explain: One complete cycle includes the full sequence of red, yellow (amber), and green lights for all directions.

q: 47. In case of multi-lane road, overtaking is generally permitted from ............
explain: In 'Keep Left' driving systems (like Nepal/India), overtaking is standardly performed from the right side of the slower vehicle.

q: 48. At a road junction, ............ cross conflict points are severe if both are two-way roads.
explain: At a standard four-legged intersection between two two-way roads, there are a total of 24 conflict points, of which 16 are major 'cross' conflicts.
Signs that command a driver to follow a specific rule (like speed limits or stopping) are categorized as mandatory or regulatory signs.

q: 50. The maximum number of vehicles can be parked with ............
explain: Right-angle (90-degree) parking allows the most vehicles per unit length of curb, though it requires the most width for maneuvering.

q: 51. The colour of light used for visibility during fog is ............
explain: Yellow (amber) light has a longer wavelength that scatters less in fog compared to white light, providing better visibility for the driver.
